units.translation: To relate the ⟦1⟧ (686) to something like the rape of Antiope seems to me inadmissible; rather, this must find its explanation in what follows, where something is corrupt in ⟦2⟧. Theseus had, through his ⟦3⟧, created a new great Athens, a ⟦4⟧, which naturally also included the Acropolis, but not the Areopagus; out of envy at this came the Amazons, from whom Theseus had abducted Antiope, and built high bulwarks against it, precisely also on the Areopagus, from which, according to ⟦5⟧, the Persians in 480 besieged the Acropolis opposite. To obtain this sense, one must write ⟦6⟧ (Orelli) ⟦7⟧, from which a ⟦8⟧ is supplied to ⟦9⟧. Objection has also been taken to ⟦10⟧ (⟦11⟧ for it Weil); but the adverb probably points to the different present, when this city was again destroyed.
and they built a high-towered new city against this city then
⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ can be compared with ⟦3⟧ 457, ⟦4⟧ . . ⟦5⟧ 14, ⟦6⟧ 999, etc.; for ⟦7⟧ Paley compares ⟦8⟧ ⟦9⟧.
city of Ilium without a city
dear friends of a dear maiden
having mounted the rock that faces the enemy

⟦1⟧ (700) 'what inspires awe'; on ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ as opposites see ⟦4⟧; but they can also be taken together, for which Wecklein recalls ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧ (Cypria in Plato Euthyphr. 12 A) and Homer O 657 ⟦7⟧; also Sophocles Ai. 1079 ⟦8⟧.
for fear, when accompanied by shame

⟦1⟧: the future of the aorist can just as well encompass the entire future, as the aorist the entire past; to be supplied is ⟦2⟧ (⟦3⟧), and ⟦4⟧ (⟦5⟧) is added as at 220 after ⟦6⟧. For ⟦7⟧ Wecklein would like ⟦8⟧ = ⟦9⟧; but ⟦10⟧ is not found in Aeschylus (though ⟦11⟧ and the like are). ⟦12⟧ (Grotius) = ⟦13⟧ seems at least not inadmissible; but better ⟦14⟧ Weil, as with ⟦15⟧ also ⟦16⟧ stands.
